title: Sixteen-cell local bitlines cut required storage charge tenfold
idea: Derive Cs from the charge-sharing equation dV=(V/2)*Cs/(Cs+Cbl) instead of accepting a 30-40 fF bitline: split each vertical bitline into 16-cell local segments (~0.3 fF, ~1 um tall) that each drive one local gain transistor onto the global bitline. The cell capacitor then only has to swing a sub-femtofarad node.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and 3D blocker (fact 2): Cs=0.5 fF still yields ~300 mV of signal versus ~5 fF today, so lateral or planar capacitors in 3D tiers become sufficient; ~10x less charge per cell also cuts restore energy.

title: Tier-wide buried back-gate plane pulsed negative during retention
idea: Deposit a continuous conductive back-gate plane under each tier's lateral access-transistor layer; during idle a charge pump holds it near -1 V, raising every access transistor's Vt through body coupling, and returns only the tier being accessed to 0 V.
why: Leakage physics: subthreshold current falls one decade per ~70 mV of Vt, so a ~300 mV coupled shift gives ~4 decades lower tail leakage (fact 3), stretching refresh from 64 ms toward minutes and removing most of the 16-33% idle refresh power; the plane costs one deposition per tier, not area.

title: Cubic mats with sense amplifiers at the array centroid tier
idea: Build each mat as a 64x64x64 cube instead of a 512x512 square and place its sense amps and local I/O in the middle tier, so every cell is at most 32 lateral pitches plus 32 tier pitches from its amplifier.
why: Energy per bit moved scales with wire length: mean path grows as N^(1/3) in 3D versus N^(1/2) in 2D, so for a 256 kb mat intra-mat wiring CV^2 drops ~5-8x (facts 5, 10) and bitline capacitance falls with it, relaxing required Cs.

title: One sense amplifier per vertical stack, multiplexed across 32 tiers
idea: Because only one tier of a bank is activated at a time, give each vertical column of 32 tiers a single sense amplifier reached through a per-tier select transistor at the column foot, instead of one sense amp per bitline per tier.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die (fact 7): sense-amp area per bit divides by the tier count, pushing periphery toward ~5-10% of footprint and making the 26-tier break-even (fact 2) reachable with cheaper tiers.

title: AND-gated cell activates only the addressed 64-bit segment
idea: Stack a column-gated vertical transistor in series with each cell's lateral access transistor so a cell reaches its bitline only when both its wordline and its column-select line are high; a random read then disturbs only the 64 addressed cells instead of the 8 kb row.
why: Destructive read and 128x overfetch (fact 8): activation energy scales with bitlines swung, so ~5.9 pJ per useful bit falls toward ~0.05 pJ; the extra device lives in Z, preserving 4F^2, and fewer opened cells also slows row hammer (fact 9).

title: Hexagonal close-packed vertical cells reach the 3.46F2 packing limit
idea: Use cylinder-forming block-copolymer self-assembly over a coarse ArF guide pattern to place vertical channels on a hexagonal lattice, routing wordlines and bitlines along two of its three 60-degree axes so each cell occupies 2*sqrt(3)*F^2 instead of 4F^2.
why: Geometry is a hard minimum: hexagonal packing (0.907) beats square (0.785), giving ~13% more bits per area at the same F, while polymer chain length rather than EUV sets the 20-30 nm pitch, removing several of the 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4).

title: Grounded shield film between every wordline tier, deposition-defined
idea: In horizontal-wordline 3D stacks, insert a 5-10 nm grounded metal or doped-poly film between adjacent wordline tiers so aggressor field lines terminate on ground instead of on the victim's storage node or channel.
why: Row hammer (fact 9) is driven by capacitive coupling and carrier injection across wordline spacing; in 3D the vertical spacer costs one deposition, not lithographic area, so coupling can drop >10x, raising flip thresholds from ~1k toward >50k activations and retiring TRR/RFM bandwidth overhead.

title: Inductor ping-pong moves charge from closing to opening wordline
idea: Connect the wordline being closed to the next wordline being opened through a shared on-die or interposer inductor for one LC half-cycle, so the 3 V charge transfers almost entirely instead of being dumped to ground, then top off the remainder from the pump.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): direct charge sharing between equal capacitors recovers at most 50%, but a resonant half-cycle recovers ~80% of CV^2; with a ~3 V wordline swing, pumped wordline energy and charge-pump losses fall several-fold.

title: Voltage-stacked tiers reuse one supply current through four arrays
idea: Power four tier groups in series (0-1 V, 1-2 V, 2-3 V, 3-4 V) so the same current flows through each array once, with interleaved address mapping to balance activity, small push-pull regulators to absorb mismatch and level shifters at tier boundaries.
why: I^2R and conversion losses scale with current: delivering 4 V at a quarter of the current cuts PDN loss ~16x and needs ~4x fewer power TSVs and bumps, attacking the HBM TSV tax (fact 6) and power-delivery overhead.

title: Binary-coded vertical tier select replaces staircase contacts
idea: Give each tier a tiny thin-film decoder hard-wired to its own tier number and run only log2(N) true/complement address rods vertically through the stack, so selecting one of 128 tiers needs 14 rods instead of a 128-step staircase with 128 contacts.
why: Staircase area and contact etch grow O(N) with layer count while decoding grows O(log N), so periphery area (fact 7) and etch steps stop scaling with tiers, making 100+ tier 3D DRAM (fact 2) area-viable.

title: Vertical charge-coupled columns store packets without access transistors
idea: Deposit a 3D-NAND-like gate stack around a single-crystal or recrystallized channel and clock the gate tiers in three phases to shift charge packets up the column to one sense node at the top, so 128 bits share one transistor and no capacitor.
why: Leakage physics: a buried potential well loses charge only by thermal generation, far below a transistor off-state tail (fact 3), and removing the per-cell capacitor sidesteps the charge wall (fact 1); a 128-deep shift at ~1 ns per step keeps access near DRAM class while density follows tier count.

title: Millimeter mat-lets fluidically self-assembled onto logic base wafers
idea: Dice DRAM arrays into ~1 mm^2 tested mat-lets and flow them in a carrier fluid over a logic wafer with shape-matched recesses, where they self-align and solder at millions per hour, so only known-good mats enter a stack or 2.5D tile.
why: Yield follows Y=exp(-D*A): at D=0.1/cm^2, 1 mm^2 parts yield ~99.9% versus ~90% for 1 cm^2 dies, compounding across 12-16 die HBM stacks, so the 20-30% HBM yield loss (fact 6) falls to a few percent.

title: 1310 nm optical links shine vertically through stacked silicon dies
idea: Exploit silicon's transparency beyond 1.1 um: each die carries micro-emitters and Ge photodiodes aligned through the stack, so data passes vertically as light through undrilled silicon, replacing signal TSVs and their keep-out zones.
why: TSV tax (fact 6): no drilled vias means no TSV area, no keep-out, no Cu-pumping yield loss and thicker, sturdier dies; the photon-energy floor (~1 eV per detected photon) leaves headroom for ~100 fJ/bit links.

title: Sandwich bonding: sense wafer below, wordline-driver wafer above array
idea: Fabricate the cell array on a wafer with no peripheral transistors, hybrid-bond a matched low-voltage logic wafer carrying sense amps to its bitline face and a thick-oxide wafer carrying 3 V wordline drivers to its wordline face, each at ~0.5-1 um pitch.
why: Periphery 49% (fact 7) and voltage floor (fact 10): each function gets its ideal process, the array wafer drops its periphery masks, and array efficiency rises toward ~90%, with periphery built on depreciated logic lines.

title: Two-nanometer silicon channels widen the bandgap to starve leakage
idea: Thin the access channel to ~2 nm by oxidation-trimming epitaxial nanosheets so quantum confinement raises the effective bandgap by ~0.3-0.5 eV; drive current remains adequate because each cell holds little charge.
why: Leakage physics: generation and band-to-band leakage scale roughly as exp(-Eg/2kT), so +0.4 eV gives ~3 decades less tail leakage (fact 3), moving silicon refresh from 64 ms toward ~1 min without exotic oxides.

title: Stepwise adiabatic bitline restore using spare-tier capacitors as reservoirs
idea: Dedicate a few cell rows per tier as reservoir capacitors held at V/4, V/2 and 3V/4; during restore and refresh, bitlines step through these reservoirs before the final rail connection, and falling bitlines replenish them.
why: Charging a capacitor in N equal steps dissipates CV^2/(2N) instead of CV^2/2, so four steps cut bitline restore loss ~4x; with refresh at ~46 fJ/bit (fact 3) and restore dominating activation energy (fact 8), this is a direct cut using cells already in the stack.

title: Z-critical cell puts every sub-20 nm dimension in film thickness
idea: Build stacked source/sacrificial/drain layers and later replace the sacrificial layer through a slit with channel, gate dielectric and wrap gate, so channel length, oxide, capacitor gap and wordline spacing are all set by ALD or epitaxy thickness and lithography prints only features of 40 nm or more.
why: Litho and capital (fact 4): film thickness is controlled to ~0.1 nm for the cost of a deposition, so 5-7 EUV layers can fall to zero using ArF immersion, removing the single-supplier EUV chokepoint and much of the depreciation.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM with defect-routing mesh bonded to accelerators
idea: Leave a 300 mm DRAM wafer undiced, link its ~2,000 mats through a redundant on-wafer mesh that test maps around bad mats, and wafer-to-wafer bond it face-to-face to an accelerator wafer so every compute tile has DRAM within millimetres.
why: Data movement (fact 5): wire energy scales with distance, so going from mm-to-cm package traces to um bond pads drops ~3-4 pJ/bit toward ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit, and dicing, packaging, interposers and TSVs disappear.

title: 77 K re-architected array: longer bitlines, halved wordline voltage
idea: Redesign the array for liquid-nitrogen operation: copper resistivity drops ~5x and subthreshold swing falls to ~15-20 mV/dec, so bitlines can be 2-4x longer with fewer sense amps, Vt can drop ~0.3 V and wordline boost shrinks from ~3 V to ~1.5 V.
why: kT physics: retention grows by many decades (refresh nearly vanishes, fact 3), CV^2 falls ~4x (fact 10) and sense-amp count halves (fact 7); honestly net-positive only after ~10x cryocooler overhead, so it targets large pooled-memory racks.

title: Correlated double sampling sense amps read 0.2 fF cells
idea: Sample the bitline before and after charge sharing onto two capacitors in a logic-process sense amp and amplify the difference, cancelling offset and 1/f noise so the required signal approaches the sqrt(kT/C) floor instead of a 6-sigma mismatch margin.
why: First principles: sqrt(kT/C) for a 30 fF bitline is ~0.37 mV, so ~3 mV suffices versus ~80-100 mV today; Cs can fall from ~5 fF to ~0.2-0.5 fF, dissolving the charge wall (fact 1) and enabling lateral capacitors in 3D (fact 2).

title: Logic-on-top stacking keeps DRAM tiers cool, with per-tier refresh
idea: Flip the HBM-style stack so the hot logic die sits against the heatsink and DRAM tiers hang below it, and embed a thermal diode in every tier that sets that tier's own refresh interval.
why: Leakage is Arrhenius (Ea ~0.6 eV), about 2x per 10 C, so running DRAM 15-20 C cooler cuts refresh rate 3-4x (fact 3), and per-tier refresh stops the whole stack refreshing at the hottest tier's rate.

title: Mirror-twin tiers interleave bitlines so the idle twin provides reference
idea: Fabricate tiers in mirrored pairs above and below one shared bitline layer whose lines alternate between serving the top tier and the bottom tier; when the top tier fires, each neighbouring bitline belongs to the idle bottom tier and acts as a perfectly matched reference.
why: Recovers folded-bitline noise rejection (~2x effective signal) inside a 4F^2 open geometry, lowering required Cs (fact 1), and halves bitline layers and sense-amp rows per tier pair (fact 7) at no area cost.

title: Convert depreciated 3D NAND lines into stacked-DRAM tier fabs
idea: From a first-principles count of process steps, a 3D DRAM tier stack is mostly deposition, high-aspect-ratio etch and replacement-metal steps, the same tool mix as 3D NAND; retrofit NAND lines idled by oversupply with DRAM-specific modules (capacitor dielectric, anneal) instead of building greenfield fabs.
why: Capital intensity and time: reusing ~60-70% of installed tools cuts capex per wafer start ~2-3x and lead time from 3-5 years to ~1-2 years, attacking the $15B+ fab barrier.

title: Area-cheap foil cells: planar 8 fF capacitors without high aspect
idea: Fabricate 1T1C arrays roll-to-roll on polyimide by UV nanoimprint at ~1 um features, using a flat 1 um^2 metal/AlOx(10 nm, spatial ALD)/metal capacitor per cell and a printed oxide TFT access device.
why: Cost per area from first principles: processed DRAM wafers cost ~$100k/m^2 versus ~$20-100/m^2 for R2R films, so the area that forces 60-75:1 pillars (fact 1) becomes nearly free; C=eA/d gives ~8 fF on a flat plate, a 10 cm^2/Vs TFT charges it in ~5-10 ns, and one layer holds ~60 GB/m^2.

title: Plywood memory: laminate 100 printed DRAM foils with edge microvias
idea: Test each 25 um printed DRAM foil, laminate 100 known-good foils with B-stage adhesive, then UV-laser drill and silver-paste fill vias through a peripheral via field to a shared bus, with each foil carrying a printed tier-select switch.
why: 3D integration without a fab: each added layer costs a lamination, not a deposition cycle, so a 10x10 cm, 2.5 mm block holds ~60 GB, and layer count passes the 26-tier break-even (fact 2) with zero EUV (fact 4).

title: Sliced laminate edge face exposes every bitline for side contact
idea: Laminate printed array foils, saw the block perpendicular to the bitlines and polish the cut face so every bitline of every foil appears as a dot at ~25 x 10 um pitch, then print redistribution or bond an edge-mounted silicon sense die directly onto that face.
why: Removes vertical vias entirely: a 10 cm x 2.5 mm edge face offers ~1M contacts, giving each bitline a direct sub-cm path to a silicon sense amp, so periphery (fact 7) lives off-foil on dense silicon while the foil stays pure array.

title: Micro-transfer-printed silicon sense amplifiers dot a printed array foil
idea: Make 50x50 um sense-amp and decoder chiplets on a depreciated logic line, release them by undercut etch, and pick-and-print thousands per elastomer-stamp cycle onto the foil, one chiplet per ~1k x 1k printed sub-array.
why: Puts the speed- and matching-critical periphery (49%, fact 7) in silicon while the array stays at R2R cost; since transistor matching sets sense margin, silicon sense amps let printed cells hold less charge and reach ~10-30 ns access.

title: EHD jet-printed pillar capacitors grown upward, never etched
idea: Use multi-nozzle electrohydrodynamic jet printing to stack silver nanoparticle droplets into 0.5 um-wide, 5 um-tall pillars on each cell's storage pad, then coat them with spatial-ALD AlOx and a conformal printed counter-electrode.
why: Additive growth escapes the aspect-ratio-dependent etch limit behind the charge wall (fact 1): C=eA/d over a 0.5x5 um pillar with 8 nm AlOx is ~80 fF, ~15x today's Cs, allowing ~10x longer bitlines and far fewer sense amps per foil.

title: Sol-gel gallium oxide printed channels give day-scale retention
idea: Inkjet or slot-die print Ga2O3 sol-gel channels (Eg ~4.8 eV), densify them by deep-UV photo-annealing below 250 C, and use them as access transistors in foil arrays with 4k-cell bitlines, since refresh traffic disappears.
why: Leakage scales as exp(-Eg/2kT), so at 4.8 eV intrinsic generation is negligible; with defect-limited off-current ~1e-21 A an 8 fF cell loses 10% only after ~days, removing refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) and going beyond the IGZO already studied.

title: Multi-height imprint stamp encodes all cell layers, zero web overlay
idea: Imprint one resist layer with a 4-5 level stamp whose heights encode gate, channel, via and capacitor patterns, then pattern each layer by successive etch-backs that expose the next height, so every level is self-aligned by the stamp itself.
why: First principles: PET expands ~20 ppm/C, so 1 C across a 30 cm web is ~6 um of misregistration, making overlay the true R2R density limit; encoding overlay in the stamp enables sub-um cells with one stamp instead of a mask set (fact 4).

title: Hot-embossed polymer trenches give 3D capacitors without plasma etch
idea: Emboss 5:1 trenches at 1 um pitch into a COC or polyimide web with a nickel-shim roller, conformally coat metal/AlOx/metal by spatial ALD and fill with printed conductor, giving each cell a folded capacitor.
why: Area multiplication is ~1+2*AR, so ~10x capacitor area per footprint from one roller pass: ~80 fF per 1 um^2 cell or 8 fF in 0.1 um^2, the 3D capacitor that wafer fabs must etch at 60-75:1 (fact 1).

title: Coextruded 500-layer polymer film forms stacked capacitor plates in one pass
idea: Use microlayer coextrusion (layer-multiplier dies proven on ~800-layer optical films) to make alternating conductive-polymer/dielectric-polymer laminates, imprint a trench grid that segments the stack into per-cell capacitors, and contact odd and even plates on opposite sidewalls after selective lateral recess.
why: Layer count is nearly free in coextrusion: C=N*eA/d with 500 layers of 50 nm, k=3 gives ~250 fF per um^2 footprint, so the tier count of fact 2 arrives in one extrusion pass rather than hundreds of deposition cycles.

title: Self-referencing double read cancels printed transistor threshold scatter
idea: Read each printed cell, write a known '1', read again through the same bitline and sense amp, compare the two samples, then restore the original data, so the cell's own capacitor and TFT threshold become its reference.
why: Printed TFT Vt scatter (~100-300 mV) and +/-20% capacitor variation would collapse a fixed-reference sense margin; self-reference turns cell variation into common mode, tolerating ~10x worse variability at ~2x read time (~40-60 ns).

title: Spiral-wound memory foil around a silicon logic spindle
idea: Wind a 10 m x 5 cm printed DRAM foil around a 1 cm logic core like a film capacitor, Schoop-spray metal onto the roll's end faces for power and plate, and route signals to pads along the foil's top edge, which land in a spiral pattern mated by an end cap.
why: Volumetric first principle: 0.5 m^2 of 25 um foil at ~60 GB/m^2 fits in a ~2.2 cm-diameter roll (~30 GB) with every cell within 2.5 cm of an end face (printed Ag line RC ~60 ps), giving capacity with no stacking tools.

title: Zig-zag folded printed sheet: continuous traces cross folds, no vias
idea: Print one long sheet of 64 array panels separated by fold lines, encapsulate the traces at the bending neutral plane, and accordion-fold it into a 64-tier stack whose tier buses run continuously across every fold.
why: Bending strain e=y/R vanishes at the neutral plane, so 12 um films can fold at ~50 um radius without cracking traces; 64 tiers (above the 26-tier break-even, fact 2) need zero vias, zero bonding and zero alignment steps.

title: DUV photo-annealed printed oxide memory tiers atop finished logic dies
idea: Nanoimprint and inkjet-print metal-oxide TFT DRAM tiers directly on a finished logic wafer's passivation, converting sol-gel films with 185/254 nm UV below 150 C so the 400 C back-end budget is never approached, in an advanced-packaging house.
why: Data movement (fact 5): memory sits micrometres above the compute it feeds, so wire energy for the hot working set falls ~10-30x versus HBM's 3-4 pJ/bit, without hybrid bonding or a DRAM fab.

title: Rolling probe-wheel test and laser-fuse repair inline on the web
idea: Run each printed array web under a roller probe that contacts test pads at line speed, measure every mat's retention and margin, and immediately laser-cut printed fuses to remap failing mats to ~3% spares before lamination.
why: Poisson yield Y=exp(-D*A) with printed defect densities of ~10/cm^2 still gives ~99% for 0.001 cm^2 mats, so cheap spares rather than cleanroom class set yield, keeping cost per bit near the raw R2R area cost.

title: Core-shell BaTiO3-alumina ink: printed high-k with leakage-blocking shells
idea: Formulate an ink of ~30 nm BaTiO3 nanoparticles each wrapped in a 2 nm Al2O3 shell, then print and compact a 60 nm dielectric, so high-k cores raise capacitance while continuous shells block grain-boundary leakage paths.
why: C=eA/d: a composite k of ~40-60 approaches the k~70 called for in fact 1 with a printable, low-temperature dielectric, letting foil cells shrink ~5x in area at equal charge.

title: Inverse-opal printed electrodes multiply capacitor area twentyfold
idea: Convectively assemble 200 nm polystyrene spheres into embossed cell wells, infill electroless nickel, burn out the spheres, then coat spatial-ALD AlOx and infill a conductive-polymer counter-electrode, forming a sponge capacitor per cell.
why: Interface area per volume of an FCC inverse opal is ~2.2/r, about 2e7 per metre, so a 2 um-thick cell holds ~40x its footprint in plate area; even derated, ~20x more capacitance per um^2 with no etch (fact 1).

title: Printed liquid-silane ink laser-crystallized into polysilicon periphery
idea: Print cyclopentasilane ink only for decoder, wordline-driver and sense circuits, convert it to amorphous silicon and excimer-laser crystallize it to ~100 cm^2/Vs polysilicon, while the cell access devices stay wide-gap oxide.
why: Drive current scales with mobility, so periphery runs ~10x faster than oxide TFTs, letting a fully printed foil reach ~20-50 ns access; it also avoids Czochralski wafers and their Spruce Pine quartz-crucible chokepoint.

title: Light-addressed foil cells: optical row strobes replace wordline drivers
idea: Give each printed cell an access TFT whose gate is charged by a small printed photodiode, and address rows by flashing a micro-LED line array beneath the transparent foil, so no metal wordline or high-voltage driver exists.
why: Wordline CV^2 at ~3 V (fact 10) and driver periphery (fact 7) vanish; a 2 fC gate charge needs ~12,500 photons, ~4 fJ per cell; speculative because printed photodiodes must respond within ~10 ns.

title: Capacitively coupled pads signal between laminated foils without vias
idea: Print 50x50 um pads facing each other across the 2 um adhesive between laminated foils and drive them with pulse signaling into a receiver, so tier-to-tier signals cross by AC coupling instead of drilled vias.
why: C=eA/d gives ~33 fF per pad pair against ~10 fF of receiver load, about 75% signal coupling, and pads tolerate the ~25 um registration of R2R lamination, removing via drilling, fill and their yield loss from foil stacks (the foil analogue of fact 6).

title: Retrofit US flexible-packaging converting lines into memory-foil fabs
idea: Partner with U.S. label and flexible-packaging converters, whose vacuum web metallizers, slot-die coaters and gravure units already run at km per hour, add enclosed ISO-5 web paths plus nanoimprint and spatial-ALD modules, and sell memory foil per square metre under a tolling model.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: a converted line costs ~$20-100M versus $15B+ for a DRAM fab, uses no EUV, no Czochralski wafers (no quartz-crucible chokepoint) and little helium, and can start within ~18 months in existing U.S. plants.

title: Milestone prize ladder for printed DRAM foils reaching $1/GB
idea: Fund a federal prize ladder paid on independent testing: about $10M for a 1 Gb printed foil with 64 ms retention, $50M for under-100 ns access with 1e15-cycle endurance, and $200M for packaged modules under $1/GB built on U.S. R2R lines.
why: Targets the physics gates (retention, speed, endurance) rather than picking a technology, pulling many teams into the area-is-cheap regime that bypasses EUV (fact 4) and fab capital; money flows only on measured results.

title: Etched-anodized aluminum foil substrate is the shared capacitor plate
idea: Borrow the electrolytic-capacitor recipe for the array substrate: tunnel-etch aluminum foil for ~50x surface area, anodize ~10 nm of Al2O3, then print each cell's conductive-polymer storage electrode and oxide TFT on top, with the foil itself as common plate, ground shield and heat spreader.
why: Low-voltage electrolytic foils already exceed ~10 uF/cm^2, i.e. ~100+ fF per um^2, so charge is abundant (fact 1) on a substrate made today by the kilometre, with anodization as a cheap wet R2R step.

title: Print coarse, heat-shrink fine: shrink-film substrates compress cells sixfold
idea: Print the array at 2.5 um features on biaxially pre-strained polyolefin or polystyrene shrink film, then heat it so the web contracts ~60% linearly, compressing cells to ~1 um while rigid oxide films buckle into controlled wrinkles that add capacitor area.
why: Cheap printing resolution sets density; a 2.5x linear shrink gives ~6x more bits per m^2 without finer tools, and wrinkling adds plate area for free (fact 1); the risks are cracking and registration under shrink.
